selection_rate.description: Fraction of population selected as parents each generation.

elitism_rate.description: Fraction of the population carried over verbatim each generation, bypassing crossover, mutation, and filters. Must be less than selection_rate. Redundant on paper under either NSGA-II scheme, whose (mu+lambda) survivor step is already elitist, and kept at 0.1 for wall time alone: the only measured difference is that 0 costs 4.0% more, yield and quality being level.

accumulate_repairs.description: Report every candidate that passed the output gate in any generation, not only the ones the final population still holds, deduplicated and unioned with the final collection before the final filters run. On by default since 2026-08-25, on the 2026-08-19-accumulator campaign: over 200 paired TLSF runs it gained implies_ideal on 6 pairs and lost it on none (exact McNemar p = 0.0312) for a median paired wall ratio of 1.034. That campaign made it a candidate default subject to a FRETISH replication that has not been run, so an archived config that omits the key now means something it did not. Free on the FRETISH path, whose per-generation realizable counter already asks the gate; on the TLSF path it adds one gate sweep per generation. Inert under tlsf.repair_mode = 'muc', which evolves cores rather than whole specifications. With the key on, each newly accumulated specification is also written to <output-dir>/accumulated/ as it is found, closed on the spot so a run killed by a wall-clock cap keeps what it had accumulated; those are raw gate-passing candidates, and repair_N.json / repair_N.tlsf remain the run's filtered output.

termination.description: Which budget ends the search. 'generations' is PEREDUR's own: the [genetic] generations rounds, whatever they cost. 'individuals' is AuRUS's, for a head-to-head where both tools get the same number of offspring rather than the same wall clock -- its GA stops once numberOfVisitedIndividuals reaches GA_MAX_NUM_INDIVIDUALS, counted per offspring admitted to the new population and checked between offspring rather than at a generation boundary. generations still bounds the run under 'individuals', as GA_GENERATIONS does for AuRUS, and max_wall_s is honoured under both. Requires max_individuals >= 1.

max_individuals.description: Offspring budget for the whole run under termination = 'individuals'; ignored under 'generations'. An offspring counts only when it differs from the parent it was bred from, matching what AuRUS counts. Zero is rejected under 'individuals' rather than meaning unlimited.

max_wall_s.description: Wall-clock deadline for the whole run in seconds; 0 is no deadline. Independent of termination and honoured under both. The search stops at the first generation boundary or bred offspring past the deadline and then writes its output normally, which is why this beats the harness's external kill: a killed run leaves no run.json and is censored with nothing recorded, where a run that stops itself reports what it found and which budget ended it. Measured from the same origin as the manifest's wall_s. Filters, scoring and the final realizability gate are not interrupted, so a run overruns by whatever the generation it was in had left.

selection_scheme.description: Selection scheme, named for its survivor step: 'nsga2-truncate' ranks the (mu + lambda) pool by Pareto non-domination and crowding distance over the individual fitness components, then truncates it at population_size; 'nsga2-apportion' (default) ranks identically but deduplicates the pool first and apportions the population_size slots over the distinct survivors by 1 / (1 + rank) under the largest-remainder (Hamilton) method; 'weighted' ranks by the weighted-average fitness scalar, but converges prematurely and is retained for comparison. Spelled 'nsga2' and 'nsga2-replicate' before 2026-08-06; those spellings are rejected, so reproduce an archived campaign at the commit its PROVENANCE.json names.

weight_syntactic.description: Syntactic similarity component weight. The defaults match AuRUS's Settings.java: 0.1 syntactic, 0.2 semantic (its lost and won models at 0.1 each) and 0.7 status.

status_grading.description: How the status objective grades below realizability: 'tiered' is the three-point scale (some component unsatisfiable, unrealizable, realizable and well-separated); 'mrs' (default) replaces the middle tier with the greedy maximal-realizable-subset fraction, admitting guarantee-side parts in spec order and scoring the fraction kept. Mrs costs more realizability queries per candidate -- a median 1.15x paired wall time -- and grades a region 'tiered' collapses to a single value; the 2026-08-11 campaign measured it at 410/480 repairs against tiered's 367/480. 'aurus' is AuRUS's own six-level ladder (0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1.0), graded by which side of the specification is satisfiable on its own; it is the only scale that does not fold well-separation into its realizability query, because AuRUS never asks that question, and it exists for an ablation against the design peredur derives from.

mrs_admission_order.description: Which order the MRS walk admits guarantee-side parts in, read only under status_grading = 'mrs'. 'spec' is the specification's own index order. 'degree' (default) admits parts by ascending pairwise-conflict degree, so a part that cannot be held with most of the others is deferred rather than blocking them; it costs n(n-1)/2 + n subset queries once, before the search starts. Both are constant across a run, which is what the walk needs for seed reproducibility and for RealizabilityChecker's cache. Measured over populations of mutants across six TLSF specifications, degree scores 0.587 against spec order's 0.529 at 1.02x the ltlsynt execs.

p_trigger.description: Per-requirement probability of mutating the trigger.

p_response.description: Per-requirement probability of mutating the response.

p_timing.description: Per-requirement probability of mutating the timing.

p_condition_type.description: FRETISH only: per-requirement probability of moving the condition type along its implication order (Continual strengthens, Trigger weakens).

p_scope.description: FRETISH only: per-requirement probability of moving the scope along its implication order. Needs a declared mode to reach any non-Global scope.

p_stop.description: FRETISH only: per-requirement probability of rewriting the stop condition of an until or before timing. Draws nothing on a requirement without one.

p_monotone.description: Both modes: probability that a rewrite takes the monotone form, whose result is comparable to what it replaces under implication. On the FRETISH path it is offered inside the condition and response rewrites and takes the requirement's own direction; on the TLSF path it is offered ahead of the temporal and propositional rewrites, its direction a fair coin.

p_add_assumption.description: Both modes: probability a mutation appends a new environment assumption (fairness over an input) instead of rewriting an existing requirement/formula.

p_remove_guarantee.description: Both modes: probability a mutation deletes one guarantee instead of rewriting a requirement/formula. The mirror of p_add_assumption; never removes the last live guarantee. Set to 0 to reproduce a run from before the operator existed.

p_conditional_assumption.description: Of the appended assumptions, the fraction guarded by a random input atom rather than by 'true'.

p_assumption.description: Probability of mutating an assumption-side section (INITIALLY/REQUIRE/ASSUME); the guarantee side (PRESET/ASSERT/GUARANTEE) takes the complement.

p_temporal.description: Probability that a chosen section formula is rewritten by the temporal-structure mutation (may insert/drop/swap X/F/G/U/R/W) rather than the skeleton-preserving propositional rewrite.

p_clone_assumption.description: Of the assumptions p_add_assumption appends, the fraction that copy an existing live ASSUME conjunct rather than build one from the template; ordinary mutation then edits the copy. Falls back to the template when there is nothing live to copy.

max_assumption_width.description: Widest disjunction tlsf_add_assumption may draw for an appended assumption's body: the body is a disjunction of between 1 and this many distinct input literals, the width drawn uniformly. A single literal was all it could draw before 2026-08-25, which put lift's ideal G F (b1 | b2 | b3) off the grammar rather than merely far from it. At 1 no width is drawn, so the RandomSource stream is what it was before this existed and an archived campaign reproduces byte for byte at that value. Values above the input count are clamped to it. It defaults to 1, its no-op value: the case for 3 is argued from the corpus rather than measured, so the operator stays off until experiments/assumption-reach decides it.

p_bare_assumption.description: Probability that an appended unconditional assumption is left as F body rather than wrapped as G F body. Every appended assumption was G-wrapped before 2026-08-25, which made a bare eventuality unreachable rather than unlikely: examples/lily11's whole ideal is F req, and G F req is strictly stronger. Read before the RandomSource is touched, so 0 costs no draw. It defaults to 0, off until experiments/assumption-reach decides it, the case for a positive value being argued rather than measured.

repair_mode.description: Repair strategy: 'monolithic' (default) evolves the whole specification at once; 'muc' extracts a minimal unrealizable core, evolves only that sub-specification, reintegrates it with the untouched non-core guarantees, and repeats.

muc_max_iterations.description: muc mode only: cap on the outer extract-repair-reintegrate loop.

default_bound.description: Trace-length bound k for bounded model counting.

metric.description: How trace counts become a similarity score: 'direct' takes the ratio of counts (a true overlap, but bound-dependent); 'logarithmic' (default) takes the ratio of their logarithms, comparing growth rates and staying stable as the bound grows.

black_timeout_ms.description: Timeout per black SAT query in milliseconds.

ltlsynt_timeout_ms.description: Per-call ltlsynt realizability timeout in milliseconds. Default 10000; 0 is no timeout. A call exceeding it is killed and reported as undecided, which does not admit a repair and drops the candidate at the well-separation filter. It was 500, on the measurement that call durations are bimodal (95% finish under 50 ms, and a 500 ms cap abandons within 0.1% of what a 10 s cap does) -- a per-corpus statistic that hides the per-specification failure: where a specification's own realizability query exceeds the budget it loses not 0.1% of its calls but all of them, and even a correct repair is rejected at the final gate. The startup budget screen warns when the input specification is in that position.

ltl2tgba_timeout_ms.description: Per-call ltl2tgba automaton-construction timeout in milliseconds. Default 60000; 0 is no timeout. Looser than the ltlsynt budget because a legitimate determinisation can take tens of seconds. A call exceeding it drops the individual against max_scoring_failure_rate.

ltlfilt_timeout_ms.description: Per-call ltlfilt simplification timeout in milliseconds. Default 10000; 0 is no timeout. An abandoned call returns the formula unsimplified rather than failing.

parallel.description: Thread pool size. Omit to use the hardware concurrency, narrowed by the CPU affinity mask and the cgroup CPU quota.

max_scoring_failure_rate.description: Fraction of a generation whose fitness scoring may throw before the run aborts. A single failure per generation is always tolerated. Default 0.15, because the ltl2tgba budget drops individuals by design and enough land in one generation on the heavy TLSF specifications to trip a tighter bound.

dashboard.description: Stream progress to <output-dir>/progress.jsonl and copy the live dashboard page beside it. Off by default; --dashboard also enables it.
